diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume $B$ is a matrix, and let $x$, $y$, and $b$ be three vectors, such that $x \in \spand(B^{\perp})$, and $b=(x+y)\gamma$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof first (correctly) writes the Gram matrix as diag(B^TB, gamma^2||x+y||^2) + [[0, gamma B^Ty],[gamma y^TB, 0]], but then replaces it by diag(B^TB,1) + [[0, gamma B^Ty],[gamma y^TB, gamma^2||x+y||^2]], which equals the Gram matrix plus e_{n+1}e_{n+1}^T; the asserted equality is false. Weyl's inequality applied to the true decomposition gives only lambda_min([B,b]^T[B,b]) >= min(sigma_min^2(B),0) + lambda_min(A) = lambda_min(A) <= 0, not sigma_min^2(B)+lambda_min(A). The stated bound is false: take B=e_1 (m=2), x=0, y=e_1, gamma=1 (all hypotheses hold). Then [B,b]=[e_1,e_1] has kappa = infinity, while the right-hand side equals sqrt((2+1+sqrt5)/(2+1-sqrt5)) ≈ 2.62.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the theorem by a correct Weyl-type bound using the true decomposition, e.g. sigma_min^2([B,b]) >= min(sigma_min^2(B), gamma^2||x+y||^2) - gamma||B^Ty||, and rederive a corresponding (different) growth factor for item 2.
issues.overall_effect: Both items of Theorem thm:cool (the paper's general 'no assumption' condition-number growth bound and its normalized-column variant with f(B,epsilon)) are unproven and item 1 is false as stated; item 2 is derived from item 1 and inherits the failure.
issues.title: Theorem thm:cool item 1 is false: wrong Gram-matrix decomposition inflates the sigma_min lower bound
issues.why_classification: The stated inequality is false by explicit counterexample and no local fix of the argument recovers it; the section's main result and its item-2 corollary must be replaced by a materially different bound.

issues.failure_explanation: Independently of ISSUE-001, the step from item 1 to item 2 needs ||B^Ty||^2/||x+y||^2 <= (epsilon^2-1)/4, but the hypothesis bounds the unsquared ratio r by d=(epsilon^2-1)/4. For d>=1 (epsilon>=sqrt5) r<=d does not imply r^2<=d (e.g. r=d=2 gives sqrt(1+16)>epsilon). The theorem also silently needs 2sigma_min^2(B)+1-epsilon>0 for the square root to be defined; nothing in the hypotheses guarantees it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the hypothesis on the squared ratio (or restrict to 1<epsilon<sqrt5) and add the condition 2sigma_min^2(B)+1-epsilon>0.
issues.overall_effect: Item 2 of thm:cool is not implied by item 1 under the stated hypothesis for epsilon >= sqrt5 and is ill-defined when 2sigma_min^2(B)+1 <= epsilon.
issues.title: Item 2 of thm:cool: hypothesis on the ratio does not imply the needed bound on the squared ratio; positivity of denominator not ensured
issues.why_classification: A local change of hypothesis fixes the inference without changing the method or conclusion (independent of the item-1 failure).

issues.failure_explanation: Letting alpha->0 in the integral definition (I_{M-1}(alpha x) ~ (alpha x/2)^{M-1}/Gamma(M)) and substituting u=x^2/2 gives Q_M(0,beta)=Gamma(M,beta^2/2)/Gamma(M), consistent with Q_M(0,beta)=P(chi^2_{2M}>beta^2). The stated formula Gamma(M,beta^2)/Gamma(M) is inconsistent with the main definition and with the chi-squared interpretation used in Theorem thm:Malcum-Bessel.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace beta^2 by beta^2/2 in the alpha=0 formula.
issues.overall_effect: Any numerical evaluation of Corollaries cor:golden2 and cor:golden3 via the stated closed form is wrong (wrong tail probabilities); the symbolic statements via Q^{ma}(0,·) remain correct.
issues.title: Marcum-Q value at alpha=0 misstated (missing factor 1/2 in incomplete gamma argument)
issues.why_classification: Single local correction; no result's statement or proof structure changes.

issues.failure_explanation: P_B^perp projects onto a subspace of dimension m - rank(B). Theorem thm:projected-noise (the only available proof route; none is given) yields parameter (m-rank(B))/2, which equals (m-n)/2 only if B has full column rank. For rank-deficient B the stated formula is false (e.g. B=0 gives ||Y||, chi-squared with m degrees of freedom).

failure_location.quote: Let \( B \) be an \( m \times n \) matrix with \( m \geq n \), and \( Y \in \mathbb{R}^m \) be a random vector with i.i.d. components

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add 'B has full column rank' (or replace n by rank(B)).
issues.overall_effect: The corollary is false without the full-column-rank hypothesis; its uses in thm:noise-ls (with B=Q^perp) satisfy the missing hypothesis.
issues.title: Corollary cor:golden3 omits full column rank; degrees of freedom m-n wrong for rank-deficient B
issues.why_classification: Standard local hypothesis addition; all downstream uses already satisfy it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:projected-noise}, with \( m-n \geq 100 \), \( \sigma = 2^{-8} \), and \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{10} \)
The probability that the norm of \( X + P_{Q}^{\perp}(Y) \) exceeds \( \varepsilon \) is given by \( \mathcal{Q}^{ma}_{(m-n)/2}\left(\frac{\|X\|_2}{\sigma},\frac{\varepsilon}{\sigma}\right) \)

issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions of thm:projected-noise allow any X in span(Q^perp), including X=0. For X=0, m-n=100, the probability equals P(chi^2_100 > (epsilon/sigma)^2) = P(chi^2_100 > 655.36), which is astronomically small (E||P^perp Y||^2 = 100*2^{-16} ≈ 0.0015, so ||P^perp Y|| ≈ 0.039 < 0.1). No proof is given and no lower bound on ||X|| is assumed, so the claimed 0.9734 is false as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis on ||X|| (or change m-n, sigma, epsilon) so that Q^{ma}_{(m-n)/2}(||X||/sigma, epsilon/sigma) >= 0.9734 actually holds, and supply the computation.
issues.overall_effect: The illustrative corollary about 'how substantial the probability can be for tall matrices' is incorrect for the stated parameters.
issues.title: Corollary cor:added-1 numerical claim is false and unproven
issues.why_classification: The statement is false and must be restated with different quantitative content, but it is self-contained with no dependents and a corrected version follows from Theorem thm:projected-noise.

issues.failure_explanation: Z_1 and Z_2 are norms; it is Z_1^2/sigma^2 ~ chi^2_n and Z_2^2/sigma^2 ~ noncentral chi^2, so the noncentral-F variable is (Z_2^2/(m-n))/(Z_1^2/n). The event Z_2/Z_1 >= eps_2/eps_1 corresponds to this F-variable exceeding n*eps_2^2/((m-n)*eps_1^2), not n*eps_2/((m-n)*eps_1) as stated. Moreover the proof shows the probability is 1 - P(F < t) yet writes it as F'(t;lambda) with F' never defined (if F' is the CDF, a '1-' is missing). The formula also breaks for the allowed eps_1=0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define F' as the noncentral-F survival function and replace the argument by n*eps_2^2/((m-n)*eps_1^2) (with eps_1>0) in the theorem and both corollaries.
issues.overall_effect: The exact probability in thm:noise-ls is misstated, and the same wrong expression is carried into the probability bounds of cor-main and cor:added-2.
issues.title: Theorem thm:noise-ls: norms treated as chi-squared variables, giving wrong F' argument (unsquared ratio) and undefined F'
issues.why_classification: Forced local correction of the formula; the method, conclusion type and all dependents survive with the corrected expression.

issues.failure_explanation: The two displayed lines are valid but distinct upper bounds (one from [B,c gamma]=[Q,c gamma]diag(R,1), the other from [B,c gamma]=[Q,c]diag(R,gamma)); they are not equal in general. Example: B=Q, gamma=2, c orthogonal to Q with ||c||=1/2 gives first line = kappa([Q,2c]) = 1 and second line = 2*kappa([Q,c]) = 4. The proof establishes only the second line, while lm:cond-ls invokes the first.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace '=' by a second '<=' (state both bounds separately) and note the first follows from the factorization [B,c gamma]=[Q,c gamma]diag(R,1); use |gamma| for real gamma.
issues.overall_effect: Item 3 as stated (an equality) is false; the bound actually used later (the first line) is unproven in the text, though it follows by the same argument with gamma absorbed into c.
issues.title: Item 3 of thm:min-max-cond asserts a false equality between two different bounds
issues.why_classification: Both bounds are true and routine; only the asserted equality must be removed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $r \neq 0$ is the residual of the least squares problem ($\|r\|_2 = \min_{u} \|c - Bu\|_2$)

issues.failure_explanation: Liesen's formula (thm:strak, eq. eq:miro) uses r = residual of c against span(B). lm:cond-ls defines ||r|| as the residual of c*gamma, which is gamma times that quantity, yet plugs it into the same formula. For gamma≠1 the stated bound is wrong: e.g. c orthogonal to span(B) with ||c||=1, gamma=2 gives ||r||=2, alpha=5, alpha^2-4gamma^2||r||^2=25-64<0, so the bound is undefined while kappa([Q,c gamma]) is finite. Hypotheses r≠0 and full column rank of [B,c] needed for thm:strak are also omitted.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define ||r||=min_z||c-Bz|| (or replace gamma^2||r||^2 by ||r||^2 and 2gamma||r|| by 2||r||), and add r≠0 / full column rank.
issues.overall_effect: lm:cond-ls is false/ill-defined for gamma≠1; cor:cond-ls (gamma=1) and later results are unaffected.
issues.title: Theorem lm:cond-ls: residual defined for c*gamma but Liesen's formula requires the residual of c
issues.why_classification: A forced local correction of the definition restores the theorem; all uses set gamma=1.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows by recognizing that $\frac{1+\sqrt{1 -  \|r\|_2^2}}{ \|r\|_2}$ is a decreasing function of $\|r\|_2$, and then applying Corollary \ref{cor:cond-ls} and Theorem \ref{thm:noise-ls}.

issues.failure_explanation: On the event ||r|| >= 1/sqrt(1+rho^2), rho=eps_1/eps_2, cor:cond-ls and monotonicity give kappa([B,q]) <= kappa(B)(1+sqrt(1-1/(1+rho^2)))sqrt(1+rho^2) = kappa(B)(rho+sqrt(1+rho^2)). The stated factor eps_1*sqrt(1+rho^2) does not follow and is false: for eps_1=eps_2<1/sqrt2 it gives kappa([B,q]) < kappa(B), impossible since appending a column cannot decrease kappa, while the event has positive probability.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the factor by eps_1/eps_2 + sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2) in cor-main and correspondingly in the product of cor:added-2.
issues.overall_effect: The condition-number bounds in cor-main and the product bound in cor:added-2 (the paper's final QR result) are false as stated.
issues.title: Corollary cor-main states a wrong growth factor (epsilon_1 sqrt(1+(eps_1/eps_2)^2)), false for small epsilon_1
issues.why_classification: The stated guarantee is false and must be replaced by a quantitatively different (though comparable) factor, propagating to the final corollary; no new architecture is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume \( B \in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R}) \) with columns of norm 1, \( q\in \mathbb{R}^{m} \), such that \( \|q\|_2=1 \).

issues.failure_explanation: The vector q in the conclusion is never defined (it must be (X+Y)/||X+Y|| for thm:noise-ls's r to be the least-squares residual of q). The proof applies cor:cond-ls, which requires columns of B of norm 1 (via Claim claim:added-2 in lm:cond-ls), but cor-main assumes only full rank; without unit columns the factor max{sigma_max,1}/min{sigma_min,1} is not kappa(B) and the bound is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: Assume \( B \) is an \( m \times n \) full rank matrix \( (m > n) \) and \( X\in \mathrm{span}(B^{\perp})

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define q=(X+Y)/||X+Y|| and add the hypothesis that B has columns of norm 1.
issues.overall_effect: As stated cor-main is ill-posed (undefined q) and its proof's input hypothesis is not guaranteed; the application in cor:added-2 does satisfy unit norms.
issues.title: Corollary cor-main: q undefined and unit-column-norm hypothesis missing
issues.why_classification: Standard local additions to the statement; all uses already satisfy them.

issues.failure_explanation: At step i the matrix B=Q̂[:,1:i-1] has i-1 columns, so cor-main gives parameters F'_{m-i+1, i-1} with (i-1)eps_{2,i}/((m-i+1)eps_{1,i}); the corollary writes F'_{m-i,i} with i/(m-i) and uses unindexed eps_1, eps_2 although the events use eps_{1,i}, eps_{2,i}. The proof's displayed bound also switches from ||a_i|| to ||w_i||. The events E_i as written compare kappa of single columns Q̂[:,i], which are all 1, not kappa(Q̂[:,1:i]).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Shift indices to F'_{m-i+1,i-1}((i-1)eps_{2,i}/((m-i+1)eps_{1,i}); ...) and define E_i with Q̂[:,1:i], Q̂[:,1:i-1].
issues.overall_effect: The probability guarantee and event definitions of the paper's final corollary do not match what cor-main yields.
issues.title: Corollary cor:added-2 misapplies cor-main: wrong degrees of freedom and unindexed epsilons in the probability bound
issues.why_classification: Routine index corrections; the union-bound argument and product structure are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $a_i \in span(\hat{Q}[:,1:i-1])^{\perp}$ and $e_i$ is a random vector in $\mathbb{R}^m$
\( X\in \mathrm{span}(B^{\perp}) \subset \mathbb{R}^m= \mathrm{span}(B^{\perp})\bigoplus \mathrm{span}(B) \) and \( Y \) is a random vector

issues.failure_explanation: cor-main assumes a deterministic X and deterministic B. In cor:added-2, B=Q̂[:,1:i-1] and a_i depend on the previous noises e_1,...,e_{i-1}, so the noncentrality ||a_i||^2/sigma^2 is a random variable. P(E_i^c) equals an expectation of the conditional probability, not the displayed deterministic expression with ||a_i||; the stated lower bound on the probability is therefore not a well-defined deterministic guarantee and is not justified by cor-main without a conditioning argument (or a deterministic lower bound on ||a_i||, using monotonicity in the noncentrality).

failure_location.quote: By exclusion principle and Corollary \ref{cor-main}, we achieve that:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Argue conditionally on the history at each step (using independence of e_i from the past) and either state the bound conditionally on (a_i) or assume deterministic lower bounds ||a_i|| >= delta_i and use monotonicity of the noncentral-F survival function in the noncentrality parameter.
issues.overall_effect: The final QR-factorization guarantee (probability bound of cor:added-2) is unsupported as stated.
issues.title: Corollary cor:added-2 applies cor-main to random a_i without conditioning; probability bound depends on random quantities

These methods could potentially be applied to address the open problem of MGS analysis without any assumptions on the condition number of the input matrix.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's only algorithmic result (cor:added-2) treats a generic abstract noise model in which each new column is an exactly orthogonal vector plus i.i.d. Gaussian noise; nothing specific to MGS (its recurrence, error structure, or a justification of the noise model for MGS) appears. The conclusion asserts specific MGS implications, whereas the introduction itself only says the methods 'could potentially' be applied to MGS.
